title: Passive-region bootstrap and incremental restore validation with canary handoff
creator: Morgan Lee
description: Runbook and verification plan to bootstrap a passive region from stored snapshots and incremental logs, validate KV and tokenstore rehydration, and perform a staged canary traffic handoff gated by circuit breakers and load-shedding. Focus is on deterministic data parity checks, rehydration time budgets, safety gates (circuit breakers and health checks), and automated rollback criteria. This ticket captures automation tasks, verification checks, and scheduling for a live drill with minimal customer exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Full restore from latest full snapshot plus incremental logs completes and converges in <= 30 minutes under simulated load
Data parity: keyspace checksum parity >= 99.999% between primary and passive after initial rehydration
Canary traffic (1% of production) served from passive region meets latency SLOs: P95 < 300ms and error rate < 0.5%
Circuit breaker gating works end-to-end: if canary error rate > 1% or latency regression > 2x baseline, traffic is automatically reverted
Load-shedding thresholds validated: graceful shedding preserves tokenstore integrity and prevents cascading failures
Automated post-restore audit produces a reconciliation report and artifacts uploaded to the drill folder
run_steps: 1) Pre-drill: Notify stakeholders (Support, Sales, Security) and schedule maintenance window in Status Page.
2) Prepare passive region: ensure compute pool reserved and runtime image pinned to runtime-1.21.
3) Snapshot retrieval: pull latest full snapshot from s3://redwood-prod-snapshots/ and confirm manifest signatures.
4) Start baseline restore: ingest full snapshot into passive KV/tokenstore cluster in read-only mode.
5) Apply incremental logs: stream WAL/incremental logs up to a target cutover timestamp and verify no gaps.
6) Run parity checks: run keyspace-check script and compare checksums with primary; collect divergence samples.
7) Warm caches: trigger synthetic warmers for hottest prefixes to populate KV cache and reduce cold-start latency.
8) Health gating: run end-to-end smoke tests (auth, generation stub, embeddings) and ensure all pass at >95%.
9) Canary handoff: route 1% of traffic to passive region via smart-router with circuit-breaker enabled.
10) Monitor and evaluate: observe latency P95, error rate, request success rate, CPU/GPU utilization for 15 minutes.
11) Decision gate: if metrics within acceptance criteria, gradually increase to 10% and then revert; otherwise revert immediately.
12) Post-drill: capture logs, produce reconciliation report, and run automated rollback where necessary.
13) Retention: upload artifacts, checksums, and runbook notes to Confluence and the drill S3 folder for audits.
verification_checks: Validate WAL continuity: ensure last-applied log index between primary and passive differs by <= 5 seconds at cutover time
SLO monitoring: query metrics system for p95_latency/redwood.request by region and compare to baseline dashboard (dashboards/latency/p95)
Circuit breaker runtime test: inject 10% synthetic error into canary and confirm breaker opens and traffic reverts in <60s
Load-shedding behavior: ramp RPS by 3x for 5 minutes and confirm shedding policy rejects low-priority requests first
Data integrity sample: run spot-check on 1k hottest keys and verify value-level hashes match
Restore time budget check: total time from snapshot restore start to canary-ready state <= 30 minutes
Audit artifact verification: checksums.csv, restore.log, and reconciliation.md uploaded to s3://redwood-dr-drills/2026-03-12/<run-id>
